scroll_scene.layer0_text: The assembled machine, as a player sees it.
scroll_scene.layer1_text: Rail, skirt and pedestal in one welded body. The only surface a player ever touches.
scroll_scene.layer2_text: Backlit glass dome, capacitive keys, powered dice bowl, and the lift column that raises it.
scroll_scene.layer3_text: One-piece PET deck with four recessed tile slots. The only interior surface tiles ever touch.
scroll_scene.layer4_text: Stores a sorted row, then a one-way geared crank lifts the finished wall flush to the deck.
scroll_scene.layer5_text: Magnetic pickup wheels lift tiles face-correct out of the drum; a belt and cam head feed them on.
scroll_scene.layer6_text: Felted disc on twelve rollers. Tiles dropped through the deck land here and are swept to each drum.
scroll_scene.layer7_text: One folded steel deck carries every subassembly, so tolerances stack against a single datum.
scroll_scene.layer8_text: Toroidal transformer and the main board, in a shielded box slung under the deck.
scroll_scene.layer9_text: Every subassembly held at its own removal height. One folded steel datum, seven stacked systems, and the shell that closes over them.
